messages:
zara: Quick heads-up — thinking about renaming the routing header we use in SDKs. Current is `X-Redwood-Route` which feels verbose and collisions-y. Proposal: `X-RW-RouteIntent` (shorter, explicit). Any immediate objections from Python/TS/Go teams?

sam: I worry about breaking clients that introspect headers (esp older proxies). Can we support both for a transition window? :thinking_face:

leo: +1 on dual-support. We should also add an env flag in the SDKs to toggle the new header, default still old name for 1 release. Then flip default in next major.

maria: Console mapping needs to be updated — the quota attribution pipeline expects `X-Redwood-Route`. If we send `X-RW-RouteIntent` without a graceful migration we'll see unknown route spikes in the quota dashboard.

ankur: We can add a shim in the edge proxy to map new -> old for 30 days. That buys time for SDK releases. But we should record telemetry for when new header is observed (so console can show adoption).

zara: Good. So plan: 1) Add header toggle env/option in SDKs (py/ts/go) -> emit both headers (new + old) for two minor releases. 2) Deploy proxy shim mapping new->old. 3) Console change: add a fallback parsing step that prefers new header then old, and a small adoption metric tile. 4) After adoption hits 90% across clients, switch default to new header and remove old after 2 months.

sam: Implementation notes for SDKs: emit both like `headers = {"X-Redwood-Route": v, "X-RW-RouteIntent": v}` — simple, non-breaking. But ensure we don't duplicate in places where we canonicalize header casing. Tests failing locally show `requests` normalizes to `x-redwood-route` in Python.

leo: Good catch. We'll canonicalize to lower-case keys in tests and in runtime to avoid dupes. Also add unit test asserting both keys are present when opt-in enabled.

maria: Console: I'll add a new field in ingestion pipeline metadata called `route_header_used` (enum: old,new,both). That will let us show a sparkline with adoption. It requires a small schema bump; I'll add a backfill plan to mark historical as "old".

ankur: On quota-attribution: If we receive both headers we should prefer `X-RW-RouteIntent` (new) for attribution. If only old present, fallback. That avoids split attribution during the dual-emit window.

zara: Can someone paste a minimal code snippet we plan to ship in the Python SDK so I can paste to the migration doc?

leo: Sure — pseudo:```python
# in http_client.py
route_val = route_hint
headers = {"x-redwood-route": route_val}
if os.getenv("RW_NEW_ROUTE_HEADER") == "1":
    headers["x-rw-routeintent"] = route_val
resp = session.post(url, headers=headers, data=payload)
```

sam: For TS: same pattern. Note: Node's HTTP libs are case-insensitive too; ensure middleware doesn't merge them into a single key.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: edge-proxy/shim v2 -> staging at 2026-03-24T15:20:00Z

maria: I'll add the console tile to the rollout dashboard and a quick alert if unknown-route count > 5% after shim goes live.

ankur: Ops ask: add a header length guard; some customers pass big JSON blobs in route headers. New header name won't change that but we should log when header size > 1KB to avoid quota pipeline weirdness.

zara: Ack. I'll draft the migration doc and timeline. Target: dual-emit SDK release next week (minor), edge-shim staged immediately, console ingest change + tile shipped in parallel. After 6 weeks evaluate adoption. Thanks all! :rocket:

sam: One more thought — add a small sampling telemetry event keyed by SDK version when new header seen. Helps correlate adoption by client version.

maria: yep adding that to ingestion plan.

leo: I'll open PRs for py/ts/go with the env toggle and tests by EOD.

zara: Perfect. Closing thread for now; ping here if you hit blockers while implementing.
